output.rationale: The fix belongs in code because the two things that produced the duplicate emails are both properties of the tool contract, not of the model's judgement. First, the declared input_schema exposes only {customer_id, template, order_id}, so there is no key the backend can dedupe on; the traces show the backend *does* honour a key when one happens to be present (tr_000513 returns eml_000256 on both the event 9 call and the event 11 retry; tr_000104 returns eml_000047 twice), but because the schema never declares it, whether the model supplies one is a coin flip \u2014 and when it did not, a second real email went out (tr_000017: eml_000008 then eml_000009; tr_000050: eml_000022 then eml_000023). Making `idempotency_key` a required parameter and deriving the message_id deterministically from it removes the coin flip: the retry re-issues the same message_id and the mailer drops it. Second, `return {"message_id": ..., "delivered": True}` executes on the success path while the harness surfaces ERROR=timeout (tr_000017 event 9 at 8106ms, tr_000050 at 8548ms, tr_000513 at 14959ms, tr_000104 at 9368ms), so the agent is handed a success-shaped body stapled to an error and has no way to tell 'never landed' from 'landed, ack lost'. Catching TimeoutError and returning status="unknown" with no `delivered` and no `message_id`, plus a replay-safe `check_email_status` read, makes the indeterminate state representable. No prompt wording can fix either defect: the system prompt's 'let them know once things have been taken care of' and the pressure not to 'leave a refund request half-finished' make retry-on-unacknowledged-write the *correct* reflex, and an agent obeying a correct reflex against an unsafe contract will keep emitting duplicates. Two companion changes are out of scope for this file and must land alongside it: (a) the `send_email` tool schema in the agent config must mirror the new signature with `idempotency_key` marked required and `check_email_status` registered; (b) `services/mailer.py` must enforce dedupe on message_id server-side and expose `was_accepted(message_id)` \u2014 this diff relies on both. The same treatment is owed to `refund_execute`, which is also `external`, also has no idempotency field, and sits one step upstream of the identical retry reflex (tr_000017/tr_000050/tr_000513/tr_000104 event 6), where a duplicate is money out the door rather than mail.
output.test_note: One test proves it: `test_timeout_then_retry_with_same_key_sends_exactly_one_email`. Stub `Mailer.deliver` to record every message_id it is called with and to raise TimeoutError on the first call and succeed on the second (reproducing tr_000017 event 9 \u2192 event 11). Call `send_email(customer_id, 'refund_confirmation', 'ord_10001', idempotency_key='k1')`, then call it again with the identical arguments. Assert three things: the first return contains status=='unknown' and has no 'delivered' and no 'message_id' key (so the agent can never read a success-shaped body off a timeout), the set of distinct message_ids the mailer was asked to accept has size 1, and the mailer accepted exactly one message. Under the current code this fails on both the second and third assertions \u2014 uuid4() mints a fresh message_id per call, which is exactly the eml_000008/eml_000009 split in tr_000017.
